## Natural history notes

A small, fast-flying falcon characterized by its compact body, pointed wings, long tail, dark streaking below, and blue-gray upperparts in adult males or browner upperparts in females and juveniles. In Florida, it is mostly a winter visitor and migrant, found in open habitats such as marshes, prairies, fields, pastures, coastal dunes, mudflats, and shorelines where small birds are abundant. It feeds mainly on small birds captured in rapid flight, though it may also take large insects and occasionally small mammals, often hunting with quick low passes or sudden pursuits across open areas.
